info.name: Forgeshift WSO2 Discovery Service
info.description:
Every REST endpoint exposed by the forgeshift-wso2-discovery-service. The per-resource POSTs run a synchronous discovery for one WSO2 resource type and write a snapshot to MongoDB. The /discoveries endpoints orchestrate a bulk fan-out job. Only POST /wso2/apis is fully implemented; the rest are reserved templates that already accept the same request body once their service backend lands.

Default environment targets http://localhost:8081/discovery/v1. Switch via the `baseUrl` collection variable or attach a Postman environment.

Collection variables:
- baseUrl                Base URL including the context path (default: http://localhost:8081/discovery/v1)
- companyName            Multi-tenancy partner id (default: probestack)
- wso2Tenant             WSO2 tenant to discover (default: carbon.super)
- userEmail              Audit field, free-form (default: ops@local)
- jobId                  Captured from POST /discoveries response
- discoveryId            Captured from POST /wso2/* response (= requestTransactionId of the most recent discovery)
- requestTransactionId   Auto-generated Apigee-style id by the collection pre-request script before every request. Format: <4-char-prefix>_<companyName>_<wso2Tenant>_<yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS>. Backend requires this on every discovery POST.

exec: // Mint an Apigee-style requestTransactionId IF NONE IS SET, otherwise
// reuse the existing one — so every per-resource POST in a single
// 'discovery run' shares the same discoveryId and therefore the same
// revision number. The backend's RevisionSequenceService is
// idempotent on discoveryId; minting a fresh id per request would
// allocate a new revision per request and bump the counter by N.
// To start a new run, hit the '\u270f\ufe0f Start new discovery run'
// request (or clear the requestTransactionId collection variable).
// Reuse — same discovery run, same id, same revision.

item.name: Start new discovery run (reset transaction id)

exec: // Clear discovery-run state so the next discovery POST mints a
// fresh requestTransactionId (and the backend allocates a new
// revision). Until this is hit again, every per-resource POST
// reuses the same requestTransactionId and lands on the same
// revision — matching the Apigee 'one discovery run = one revision'
console.log('[reset] Cleared requestTransactionId, discoveryId, jobId, revision');
console.log('Next discovery POST will mint a fresh requestTransactionId and allocate a new revision.');

request.description:
One-click reset. Clears the auto-minted requestTransactionId (and discoveryId / jobId / revision) collection variables so the next per-resource POST starts a fresh discovery run with a brand-new revision. The HTTP call itself is harmless — just hits /actuator/info to give Postman something to send.

Run this whenever you want to start a new discovery run. Until you do, every POST /wso2/* in the collection reuses the same requestTransactionId so all snapshots land on the same revision — same contract as the Apigee discovery service.
Spring Boot Actuator health probe. 200 with {"status":"UP"} when Mongo is reachable.
Opens the interactive Swagger UI page. Best viewed in a browser, not Postman.

item.name: WSO2 Resources (Per-resource discovery)
item.description: Each POST runs a synchronous discovery against the source WSO2 instance, writes a snapshot per item to `discovery_wso2_<resource>`, and returns the typed detail list. Body shape is identical across endpoints. The first endpoint, /wso2/inventory, is the only one that does NOT persist or allocate a revision; it is a cheap list-only pre-flight pass.

request.description:
Cheap, list-only pre-flight pass. Acquires one OAuth token with publisher+admin+devportal scopes, then in parallel hits every list endpoint:
  - GET /api/am/publisher/v4/apis
  - GET /api/am/publisher/v4/api-products
  - GET /api/am/publisher/v4/endpoint-certificates
  - GET /api/am/admin/v4/key-managers
  - GET /api/am/admin/v4/scopes
  - GET /api/am/admin/v4/throttling/policies/{subscription,application,advanced}
  - GET /api/am/devportal/v3/applications
  - GET /api/am/devportal/v3/subscriptions

Returns summary lists per resource type. Does NOT persist to MongoDB and does NOT allocate a revision. If one endpoint fails (e.g. insufficient scope), that list is empty and an entry appears in response.errors keyed by the resource slug.

Discovers all APIs in the WSO2 tenant via the Publisher REST API v4.

Flow: acquire token → list APIs → fetch each API definition → upsert snapshots to `discovery_wso2_apis` → return apiDetails list.

Response `type` = `apis`, populated detail field = `apiDetails: ApiDetail[]`.

Discover all DevPortal Applications via GET /api/am/devportal/v3/applications.

Flow: acquire token (devportal scope) -> list applications -> upsert snapshots to `discovery_wso2_applications` -> return applicationDetails.

Response `type` = `applications`, populated detail field = `applicationDetails: ApplicationDetail[]` (id, name, owner, status, throttlingPolicy, tokenType, groupId, subscriber, subscriptionCount).

Discover app <-> API Subscriptions via GET /api/am/devportal/v3/subscriptions.

Flow: acquire token (devportal scope) -> list subscriptions -> upsert snapshots to `discovery_wso2_subscriptions` -> return subscriptionDetails.

Subscriptions are the spine of the migrator: every Consumer + credential created on the Kong side starts from a row here.

Response `type` = `subscriptions`, populated detail field = `subscriptionDetails: SubscriptionDetail[]` (id, applicationId/Name, apiId/Name/Version/Context, throttlingPolicy, status).

exec: const byType = (j.throttlingPolicyDetails || []).reduce((acc, p) => { acc[p.policyType] = (acc[p.policyType]||0)+1; return acc; }, {});

request.description:
Discover Throttling Policies across all three tier families:
  - GET /api/am/admin/v4/throttling/policies/subscription
  - GET /api/am/admin/v4/throttling/policies/application
  - GET /api/am/admin/v4/throttling/policies/advanced

Merges all three into one snapshot stream tagged with `policyType`. Required scope: `apim:admin`.

Flow: acquire token (admin scope) -> list all 3 tier families -> tag each item with its policyType -> upsert snapshots to `discovery_wso2_throttlingpolicies` -> return throttlingPolicyDetails.

Response `type` = `throttlingpolicies`, detail field = `throttlingPolicyDetails: ThrottlingPolicyDetail[]` (id, name, displayName, policyType, requestCount, dataAmount, dataUnit, timeUnit, unitTime, stopOnQuotaReach, billingPlan, isDeployed).

exec: console.log(`keymanagers: total=${j.totalCount} revision=${j.revision} types=${(j.keyManagerDetails||[]).map(k => k.name + '(' + k.type + ')').join(', ')}`);

request.description:
Discover registered Key Managers via GET /api/am/admin/v4/key-managers. Required scope: `apim:admin`.

Flow: acquire token (admin scope) -> list key managers -> upsert snapshots to `discovery_wso2_keymanagers` -> return keyManagerDetails.

Key Manager type drives downstream Kong auth-plugin choice:
  - default Resident KM (JWT)  -> Kong `jwt` plugin with WSO2 signing key
  - federated OIDC (Keycloak / Okta / Auth0 / WSO2-IS) -> Kong `openid-connect` plugin

Response `type` = `keymanagers`, detail field = `keyManagerDetails: KeyManagerDetail[]` (id, name, type, enabled, issuer, tokenEndpoint, introspectionEndpoint, jwksEndpoint, availableGrantTypes, tokenType).

Discover all API Products via GET /api/am/publisher/v4/api-products. Required scope: `apim:api_view`.

API Products bundle operations from one or more existing APIs. Each snapshot is persisted to `discovery_wso2_apiproducts`.

Response `type` = `apiproducts`, detail field = `apiProductDetails: ApiProductDetail[]` (id, name, version, context, provider, state, description, apiCount).

Discover all shared OAuth2 scopes via GET /api/am/admin/v4/scopes. Required scope: `apim:admin`.

Scopes drive Kong authorization translation: WSO2 binds scopes to roles, Kong binds them to consumer groups / ACL lists.

Each snapshot is persisted to `discovery_wso2_scopes`. Response `type` = `scopes`, detail field = `scopeDetails: ScopeDetail[]` (id, name, displayName, description, bindings, usageCount).

Discover all endpoint TLS certificates via GET /api/am/publisher/v4/endpoint-certificates. Required scope: `apim:api_view`.

Each certificate is keyed by alias and bound to a backend endpoint URL. Used downstream to populate Kong certificate + SNI objects.

Each snapshot is persisted to `discovery_wso2_certificates`. Response `type` = `certificates`, detail field = `certificateDetails: CertificateDetail[]` (alias, endpoint, subject, issuer, expiryDate, validFrom, serialNumber, version).

exec: const byType = (j.mediationPolicyDetails || []).reduce((acc, p) => { acc[p.type||'unknown'] = (acc[p.type||'unknown']||0)+1; return acc; }, {});

request.description:
Discover Mediation Policies (Synapse sequences applied to in/out/fault flows). Required scope: `apim:api_view`.

WSO2 4.x has no tenant-wide mediation-policies endpoint - policies are per-API. This call:
  1. Lists every API (Publisher v4 /apis)
  2. For each API, GET /apis/{apiId}/mediation-policies
  3. Tags each policy with apiId / apiName / apiVersion / scope=api

Cost is O(N) Publisher calls where N = number of APIs in the tenant.

Response `type` = `mediationpolicies`, detail field = `mediationPolicyDetails: MediationPolicyDetail[]` (id, name, type=in/out/fault, scope, apiId, apiName, apiVersion, shared, contentType).

Discover WSO2 users from the SCIM 2.0 user store via GET /scim2/Users. Required scope: `apim:admin` (or whichever scope the OAuth client was granted SCIM read for).

SCIM has a different response shape than the APIM REST APIs - the wrapper key is `Resources` (capital R), and pagination uses `startIndex` (1-based) + `count`.

If SCIM is gated on Basic admin auth instead of bearer tokens in your build, the call 401s and the discovery returns empty with a log warning. Grant the SCIM scope to the OAuth client (or we add a Basic-auth fallback later).

Response `type` = `users`, detail field = `userDetails: UserDetail[]` (id, userName, displayName, emails, active, roles, userType).

item.name: History & Diagnostics
item.description: Read-only history surface (history, history/revisions, history/details), the compare diff, the assetinfo write endpoint, the token-acquisition diagnostic, and stats roll-ups over the discovery data.

request.description:
List past discoveries with per-resource-type counts. Reads across all discovery_wso2_* collections and groups by (historyId, revision). Sorted by revision descending. Response mirrors the Apigee /history shape: `{ companyName, wso2Tenant, history: [{ historyId, fetchedAt, revision, summary }], processingTimeMs }`.

Optional filters:
- `resourceType` restricts which collections are scanned and what shows up in `summary`.
- `requestTransactionId` filters to one specific discovery run (matches `historyId`). Enable the disabled query param above to use it; default value pulls from the `discoveryId` collection variable set by the last discovery POST.
Returns the current revision counter (from `discovery_revisions`) plus every revision number that has at least one snapshot under (companyName, wso2Tenant).
Drill-down to the raw DiscoverySnapshot rows for one resource type. Filters by discoveryId and/or revision. Returns the full payloads, capped at `limit`.

Diff two discoveries by their discoveryIds. Returns added / removed / changed / unchanged per resource type.

Changed detection is shallow on purpose - compares a curated set of identifying fields (name, version, lifecycleStatus, status, state, enabled, throttlingPolicy, type, issuer, endpoint). Full deep-diff lands later.

Set collection variable `sourceDiscoveryId` to a prior discoveryId; targetDiscoveryId defaults to the most recent one captured by an implementation request.

Attach business-metadata (businessUnit, appId, projectName, deployableUnit) to already-discovered APIs. Writes to `probestack_wso2_asset_info` with a deterministic composite id so re-posting the same row is idempotent.

exec: console.log(`tokenTest: success=${j.success} authType=${j.tokenAuthType} elapsedMs=${j.elapsedMs} prefix=${j.tokenPrefix||'-'} error=${j.errorMessage||'-'}`);

request.description:
Diagnostic. Calls Wso2Client.acquireToken(scope) and reports success + auth-type + latency without leaking the full token (only a 6-character prefix). Scope can be `apim:api_view`, `apim:admin`, `apim:subscribe`, or the special slug `inventory` which requests the combined publisher+admin+devportal scope.

Gated by `forgeshift.wso2.token-test.enabled` (defaults to true; set to false in prod profiles).
Counts of snapshot documents per resource slug. Useful for the UI dashboard summary card.
Counts of snapshot documents grouped by (companyName, wso2Tenant). No query-param filters - intentional, this is the cross-tenant view.
One bucket per (discoveryId, revision) with snapshotAt. Drives the UI history-page table without a separate history call.
Counts per UTC day (yyyy-MM-dd). Drives a sparkline / line chart on the UI dashboard.

item.name: Admin (Profiles / Organizations / Audit / Relations)
item.description: Multi-tenancy + observability surface. Profile CRUD for onboarding tenants, plus read endpoints for the auto-maintained organizations / audit / relations collections.

request.description: Create or update a per-tenant WSO2 connection profile. Secrets are accepted as plain text but masked on every read. Composite id `{companyName}|{wso2Tenant}` makes re-posting idempotent.
Paged list. Optional companyName filter. Password and clientSecret are masked in every row.
Read one profile. Secrets masked.
Remove a profile. Subsequent discoveries for this tenant fall back to the static forgeshift.wso2.* config.
List tenants we have data for, auto-upserted by every discovery. Includes lastSeenAt / lastDiscoveryId / lastRevision / lastUserEmail per tenant - useful for the UI dashboard summary.
Read one organization row.
Read the async audit log of every REST request. Sorted by requestedAt DESC. Optional filters: companyName, wso2Tenant, status (SUCCESS / FAILED).
Single audit entry by Mongo _id.
List denormalized app <-> API relation rows. Populated by Wso2SubscriptionsDiscoveryService after each subscription discovery.
Which APIs does this application subscribe to?
Which applications subscribe to this API?

item.name: Bulk Discovery Jobs
item.description: Async fan-out across multiple resource types. The job document tracks state, the per-resource services do the work.

request.description:
Starts an async bulk discovery. Returns 201 with a job id; the worker runs on the discoveryExecutor thread pool.

`resourceTypes` is optional. If omitted, defaults to all implemented resource types.

Implemented slugs (May 2026):
  - apis
  - apiproducts
  - applications
  - subscriptions
  - throttlingpolicies
  - keymanagers
  - scopes
  - certificates
  - mediationpolicies (per-API loop, O(N) cost)
  - users (SCIM 2.0)

All planned per-resource endpoints are now implemented.

All resource-type discoveries within one bulk run share the same revision number, allocated when the first sub-discovery runs.
Reads the bulk job document. Poll for state transitions: PENDING → LISTING → COMPLETED / FAILED.
List bulk jobs, paginated. Optional filters: `state`, `companyName`, `tenant`.
Deletes the job document. Does NOT delete the snapshot documents in `discovery_wso2_*` collections.
